31.0.0.en: 1 And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the third month, in the first day of the month, that the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude; Whom art thou like in thy greatness? 3 Behold, the highest of the cedars in Lebanon, with fair branches, and with a shadowing shroud, and of an high stature; and his top was among the thick boughs. 4 The waters made him great, the deep set him up on high with her rivers running round about his plants, and sent out her little rivers unto all the trees of the field. 5 Therefore his height was exalted above all the trees of the field, and his boughs were multiplied, and his branches became long because of the multitude of waters, when he shot forth. 6 All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs, and under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young, and under his shadow dwelt all great nations. 7 Thus was he fair in his greatness, in the length of his branches: for his root was by great waters. 8 The cedars in the garden of God could not exceed him: the cypress trees were not like his boughs, and the plane trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty. 9 I have made him fair by the multitude of his branches: so that all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him."

31.0.1.en: God commands Ezekiel to ask Pharaoh of Egypt:

31.0.2.en: "Whom art thou like in thy greatness?

31.1.0.en: Behold, (Assyria) the highest of the cedars in Lebanon, with fair branches, and with a shadowing shroud, and of an high stature; and his top was among the thick boughs..." [2-3].

31.1.1.en: Whether He rebukes Pharaoh of Egypt because he exalts himself in his own eyes on account of the gifts and endowments God gave him, or presents to him Assyria, which bore the same trait of "pride," as an example for him, the picture presented applies to man, whom God has flooded with every possibility of success, but instead of glorifying God he fell into pride and so collapsed. This is a lamentation over every soul, and it approaches the lamentation over the prince of Tyre as a symbol of the devil, whom God made above every earthly and heavenly creature, a cherub in His garden bearing the throne. He hid from him none of the secrets, but when he became proud he fell.

31.1.2.en: Some see that God asks Pharaoh to think about Assyria, the great kingdom that fell. In 609 B.C. Pharaoh Necho went to Carchemish to help the Assyrian empire, which was suffering Babylonian attacks. But the efforts failed, and Assyria was torn out of history, like a cedar tree in Lebanon that has been uprooted.

31.2.s.en: And now, what has God given us?

31.2.0.en: The Lord summed up His gifts to us in three matters:

31.3.0.en: a. "Behold, (Assyria) the highest of the cedars in Lebanon" [3].

31.3.1.en: Assyria was the greatest state at that time, appearing like the lofty cedar tree; its king was greater than all the kings of the surrounding states, who were subject to him.

31.3.2.en: God created us as the most perfect earthly creature, setting us on the sixth day after He had brought all things into being for our rest. He gave us a rational soul in His image and likeness, and granted us dominion over every earthly creature. He wished not to humble him but to exalt him, not to deprive him but to satisfy him, not to make him a pliant instrument in His hand but a being with a free will... He raised him to the utmost limits.

31.3.3.en: "Thus was he fair in his greatness, in the length of his branches...

31.4.0.en: The cedars in the garden of God could not exceed him: the cypress trees were not like his boughs, and the plane trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty. I have made him fair by the multitude of his branches: so that all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him" [7-9]. He is God's planting, the work of His hands; He planted him in His garden and set him fair, fairer than all the trees of His garden, so that Satan envied him for the splendor which the Lord poured upon him, and urged him to pride and to exalt himself against God!

31.4.1.en: b. "With fair branches" [3]. Satan envied him because of the multitude of his branches [9], for "all the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs, and under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young, and under his shadow dwelt all great nations" [6].

31.4.2.en: He likens the nations subject to Assyria to birds that shelter among the branches of the tree, or like the beasts of the earth that bring forth their young under its branches.

31.4.3.en: What are these many fair branches that God gave, to shelter the fowls of heaven and for the beasts of the field to bring forth their young under its shadow, if not the nature of love that God placed in him, so that man might extend with his heart toward all mankind, and even toward every earthly creature? In him the saints find rest, and in him the suffering find rest, and to him all resort to find in him a spacious heart able to embrace many. God created man a being beloved and loving, the object of the love of God and His angels, and his heart too is made wide to love.

31.4.4.en: Truly Assyria widened by its might and authority to embrace many nations under its banner, and also Pharaoh of Egypt under its authority; but the children of God widen with true inward love so that, if possible, they love even those who oppose them and the wicked, so that all may find their rest in them.

31.4.5.en: c. His planting by the overflowing streams of water: "The waters made him great, the deep set him up on high with her rivers running round about his plants, and sent out her little rivers unto all the trees of the field" [4]. If Pharaoh drinks from the overflowing waters of the Nile, which gave him riches and wealth and upheld him in his greatness, until he was satisfied and overflowed upon the rest of the nations, sending streams of water to all the trees of the field, then in this he resembles Assyria also, which relied on the Tigris and the Euphrates... But behold, Assyria has fallen!

31.4.6.en: As for us believers, we must experience that this is the work of God's grace in us. For we are planted by the waters of holy Baptism, and are watered inwardly by the Holy Spirit, who gives us uprightness so that our stature enters into the cloud, and our branches stretch out in every direction, and this is reflected even upon others, so that they receive the work of the Spirit in them. They are kindled by His fire when they see us kindled by His holy fire, and they enjoy the work of holy Baptism when they touch its effectiveness in us.

31.4.7.en: If the height of the cedar tree until its top reaches the cloud [3] points to the life of perfection and sanctification that God gave to man, for by them he enters into the mysteries of the Kingdom and beholds the hidden divine glories, and if the multitude of branches points to the power of love by which the heart is widened for all, then both of them, "holiness and love," are the gift of the Holy Spirit who works in us through the waters of holy Baptism, for He says: "Therefore his height was exalted above all the trees of the field, and his boughs were multiplied, and his branches became long because of the multitude of waters, when he shot forth" [5]. In the waters of Baptism we sprout as a new branch in the true Vine, and by the divine Spirit we grow continually in uprightness upward and in the multitude of branches outward.

31.4.8.en: Therefore Abba St. Isaac the Syrian says: [If good is done to you, openly or secretly, be sure that Baptism and faith are the two mediators of this good, for by them you were called to good works in Christ Jesus].

31.4.9.en: And Father Methodius says: [Those who are enlightened receive the features of Christ... For He necessarily imprints on each of them the form of the Word and His image and His features, so that Christ is reckoned as born in each of them, by the action of the Holy Spirit... and those who are baptized become other christs].

31.4.10.en: As St. James of Sarug says in one of his homilies on Baptism: [Baptism writes your name above in heaven, in the church of the firstborn, and you become a son of the Father who sits on high!]

31.4.11.en: Thus the true believer combines spiritual beauty and height and loftiness, and power and love... until he surpasses all the other trees, and they even envy him.

31.5.s.en: 2. The fall of the cedar tree:

31.5.0.en: 10 "Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thou hast lifted up thyself in height, and he hath shot up his top among the thick boughs, and his heart is lifted up in his height; 11 I have therefore delivered him into the hand of the mighty one of the heathen; he shall surely deal with him: I have driven him out for his wickedness. 12 And strangers, the terrible of the nations, have cut him off, and have left him: upon the mountains and in all the valleys his branches are fallen, and his boughs are broken by all the rivers of the land; and all the people of the earth are gone down from his shadow, and have left him. 13 Upon his ruin shall all the fowls of the heaven remain, and all the beasts of the field shall be upon his branches: 14 To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height, neither shoot up their top among the thick boughs, neither their oaks stand up in their height, all that drink water: for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with them that go down to the pit. 15 Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the day when he went down to the grave I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed: and I caused Lebanon to mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted for him. 16 I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell with them that descend into the pit: and all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth. 17 They also went down into hell with him unto them that be slain with the sword; and they that were his arm, that dwelt under his shadow in the midst of the heathen. 18 To whom art thou thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? yet shalt thou be brought down with the trees of Eden unto the nether parts of the earth: thou shalt lie in the midst of the uncircumcised with them that be slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, saith the Lord GOD."

31.5.1.en: The Book of the prophet Ezekiel focuses on the sin of pride as the secret of the fall. Here he says: "Because thou hast lifted up thyself in height, and he hath shot up his top among the thick boughs, and his heart is lifted up in his height; I have therefore delivered him into the hand of the mighty one of the heathen; he shall surely deal with him: I have driven him out for his wickedness" [10-11]. God desired to see him with his stature lifted up and his top reaching within the cloud (the thick boughs), but when his heart was lifted up in his loftiness, he fell from the height of his stature and his top came down from the cloud. Many have been lifted up in their spiritual stature and entered into the hidden mysteries of God while keeping a humble heart, as happened with St. Mary. The Virgin praised God, saying: "He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree." Therefore the Fathers warned us against pride and vainglory or arrogance, as they urged us to humility.

31.5.2.en: St. John Climacus says: [Humility is the heavenly ladder that can lift the soul from the pit of iniquities to heaven].

31.5.3.en: [If the pride of some of the angels turned them into demons (Isa 14:14; 1 Tim 3:6), then without doubt humility can make angels of demons (fallen souls); therefore let those who have fallen take courage].

31.6.s.en: The fruit of pride and its work in us is:

31.6.0.en: a. Pride humbled Assyria and subjected it to Babylon, and it does the same to Pharaoh of Egypt:

31.7.0.en: "Strangers, the terrible of the nations, have cut him off" [12]. Truly the grace of God forsakes the proud man, and he becomes prey to the demons; by this these terrible strangers cut him off. But the humble man is upheld by the grace of God, and the beasts of the field submit to him, and he reigns over the earth. Therefore it was said: "Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth" (Mt 5:5).

31.7.1.en: b. The matter does not stop at the demons' raging against him, but he loses the inward traits that were given him: "Upon the mountains and in all the valleys his branches are fallen, and his boughs are broken by all the rivers of the land; and all the people of the earth are gone down from his shadow, and have left him" [12]. This is a bitter picture of the soul, for its destruction is not the result of an outward war but the result of an inward death; its branches fall after they dry up and lose all vitality wherever it is found, whether on the high mountains or in the low valleys, in the wilderness or by the rivers. His corruption springs from within him whatever the circumstances, so he becomes without branches, barren and dry, in whose shade no one takes shelter, and in whom no man finds rest, and he is left alone.

31.7.2.en: St. John Chrysostom wrote many discourses on this matter, declaring that no one can harm a man unless the man harms himself. Through pride a man shatters his life, attributing his failure to the circumstances around him or to the people who deal with him. The fault is in the tree, which bore its own dryness, not in the mountains or valleys or rivers or peoples that left it.

31.8.0.en: c. Instead of the fowls of heaven flying to him to rest in the shade of his branches, and the beasts of the field fleeing to him to bring forth their young under his shadow, it was said: "Upon his ruin (the fallen tree) shall all the fowls of the heaven remain, and all the beasts of the field shall be upon his branches" [13]. The tree became a ruin with no use in it, so the birds settle on it in contempt of it, and the animals come to it as to a place of desolation. The soul becomes a bearer of the fowls of heaven, that is, the spirit of arrogance and haughtiness, and bears the beasts of the field, or the spirit of violence, ferocity, and bestiality.

31.9.0.en: d. It falls into the abyss and becomes a warning to the other trees: "To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height... for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with them that go down to the pit" [14].

31.10.0.en: e. Man loses his joy and brings himself and those around him into sorrow: "In the day when he went down to the grave I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed: and I caused Lebanon to mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted for him. I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell" [15-16].

31.10.1.en: The soul loses the secret of its joy, for it is deprived of the rivers of holy grace, and the living waters dry up for it, so other souls grieve for it, and also tremble in fear for themselves, they who share with it in its sins.

31.11.0.en: f. He ended his discourse on the end of the proud by saying: "Thou shalt lie in the midst of the uncircumcised with them that be slain by the sword" [18]. His end is not only a hideous death, that is, being slain by the sword, but even in his lying down he is among the uncircumcised, that is, the defiled, as though he lost his life here on earth in its most hideous form, which is being slain by the sword, and loses his other life by being counted with the defiled.

31.11.1.en: Thus all greatness is lost, and all glory vanishes, and the soul is deprived of the fruit of the divine grace that was offered to it freely! This is the work of pride!

31.11.3.en: * Pharaoh of Egypt did not learn from the king of Assyria, the lofty cedar tree, which became cast on the ground.

31.11.4.en: Instead of sheltering the fowls of heaven and shading the beasts of the field, it became dry and worthless!

31.11.5.en: * Take pride away from me, O Teacher of humility!

31.11.6.en: Teach me to be planted by the waters of Your grace in Your paradise, and to bear the fruit of the true Spirit!

31.11.7.en: * I confess to You my sin and my weakness, and I thank You for the riches of Your grace in my life!

31.11.8.en: All good in me is from You, O Maker of good things.
